items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: Abbott and Costello are still funny today.

ctx.x: Well a mutual friend told me to ask you about Chico Marx.

Yeah he was special. He was special. And they were all, I mean Harpo, Chico, they were all incredibly talented. They weren’t just funny, they got it somehow. And I think the criteria for any art form is its longevity. I mean you don’t see people look at the Mona Lisa and say aah, shoulda had more blue, or looking at the Sistine Chapel and say no you should have used more reds. I mean 500 years later you look at that painting and it still takes your breath away. So the real criteria for artists is longevity. And…

one routine. And it took years to create that routine. Unfortunately today that part of the puzzle it no longer exists. Where there used to be theaters where you could work a week at Wilkes Barre, then a week in Philadelphia, a week in Pittsburgh, a week in Allentown, a week in Altoona, then you’d hit Ohio. And then after that there were supper clubs. And that was my background, working supper clubs.
